timeline.event: Audit create by i-fengyicheng; job created (8 replicas, 8 GPU each).
All eight replicas created ("Start replica") by rjob-controller.
Gang scheduling retries (76 FailedScheduling events): the eight-pod group could not be placed together; queue wait 3.53 h.
Eight pods created and started (pod startTime).
Containers begin (4 replicas at 12:17:37, four at 12:20:08-12:20:25).
Native vLLM servers launched on all eight nodes (server_started_at_utc).
Decode head (gpu-h200-0760): DP Coordinator process 1357 and 4 API servers started.

INITIATING EVENT: decode head EngineCore_DP0 logs "Address already in use. Retrying with a new port."; at the same second the three decode DP peers begin failing TCPStore handshakes against 10.204.22.14:40273. The decode engine never initializes after this line.
Contrast: prefill head (gpu-h200-0043) starts V1 engine and forms its DP group normally (world_size=8); prefill reaches /health 200 at 12:31:05.8.

All three decode peers (0819/0828/0882) retry the coordination TCPStore 39-41 times until shutdown (backoff up to ~90 s): "Failed to recv, got 0 bytes", "Connection reset by peer", and "Ping failed, invalid value returned from server. Expected: 1319, Got: 255". The four prefill logs contain zero TCPStore errors.
Decode head startup_timeout_s=1800 elapses: TimeoutError in native_pd_worker.await_condition; worker writes failed.json; process manager SIGTERMs DP0/API servers.
Head container exits 1 (API terminated: "user command: exit status 1"); peer 0882 raises "Native P/D peer failed" and exits; 0357 aborts its await_replay.
RJob finishTime; rjob-controller stops the remaining replicas (62 stop operations, no human actor); all pods deleted.
Launcher raises "Waited job ... ended with status: failed" and then calls Job Stop (20:50:53.024 HKT) - cleanup after the platform had already failed the job.

initiating_event.object: exp-1102-164536-160317-a87ff679 (decode role, lane 0, position 4), node gpu-h200-0760.lgcm.sh.istep.fun, container log of the native vLLM server
initiating_event.text: (EngineCore_DP0 pid=1495) WARNING 11-02 12:22:14 [parallel.py:655] Address already in use. Retrying with a new port.
initiating_event.corroborating_text: [W1102 12:22:14.227747612 TCPStore.cpp:125] [c10d] recvValue failed on SocketImpl(fd=84, addr=[gpu-h200-0819...]:35132, remote=[gpu-h200-0760...]:40273): Failed to recv, got 0 bytes. Connection was likely closed.
initiating_event.observation: The decode role never completed vLLM data-parallel group initialization. The head engine core reported a bind conflict and retried; its coordination TCPStore on 10.204.22.14:40273 never completed a valid handshake with the three peer lanes, /health never returned 200, and the 1800 s startup window expired.
initiating_event.code_reference: The message is emitted by vllm/config/parallel.py:655 (stateless_init_dp_group) in native_source 2cf0a6915ce544dc493a0990f2ea38d81601128a, for a DistNetworkError whose text contains EADDRINUSE; the function retries up to five times with a fresh port.
initiating_event.cause_status: UNDETERMINED - the process that caused the bind conflict is unknown, and the surviving evidence does not select external port occupancy versus internal port contention or retry behaviour.

failure_chain: Decode DP group init on the head (0760) collided on a port at 12:22:14Z and retried.
The three peer lanes 0819/0828/0882 could not complete a TCPStore ping against 10.204.22.14:40273 (0-byte reads, connection resets, and "Ping failed ... Expected: 1319, Got: 255").
Peers retried 38-41 times with exponential backoff until shutdown; no decode engine was ever initialized (no "Initializing a V1 LLM engine" line on 0760, no serving/ directory on any decode node).
Decode /health never returned 200, so native_pd_worker.await_condition(healthy, startup_timeout_s=1800, native_required=True) raised TimeoutError at 12:50:44Z (window started ~12:20:44Z).
The worker wrote failed.json and exited 1 (container exit code 1, reason Error).
Peer replicas raised "Native P/D peer failed" (0882) or aborted await_replay (0357, and others on shutdown), so all replicas ended.

The platform applied task fail policy "any" and stopped the seven remaining replicas (12:50:51-12:50:58Z); the launcher then reported the failure at 12:50:52Z and issued its own Job Stop at 12:50:53Z.

classification.verdict: UNCLASSIFIED BY CAUSE - do not use this report to authorize or deny a retry.
classification.observed_failure_mode: native data-parallel rendezvous did not complete on the decode head (EADDRINUSE plus retry, then TCPStore handshake failures with the peer lanes)
what_is_established: The decode role failed first and never initialized an engine; the prefill role formed its DP group and became healthy at 12:31:05.8Z.
The head reported EADDRINUSE at 12:22:14Z and its coordination TCPStore at 10.204.22.14:40273 never served a valid handshake to 0819/0828/0882.
The failure preceded the platform stop by about 28 minutes, and no replay or inference request ran.
what_is_not_established: Whether a process outside this workload held the port (external infrastructure occupancy) or the native stack lost a port-selection/retry race internally. Both remain open; the original occupant cannot be identified from logs because the container and its host process table are gone.
Whether the same configuration would fail again on a different node.
classification.not_preemption: preemptible=yes is only a label. The stop annotation is rjob.brainpp.cn/system-stop-reason "Task fail policy [any] caused undesired running replicas.", every replica stop is by rjob-controller with no human audit row, and the failure preceded the stop by 28 minutes.
classification.not_workload: No replay, warmup or request ever started (no replay_finished.json, no request metrics, no run/ directory). The harness fail-fast path behaved as designed.
classification.not_image_or_mount: Image pull finished at 12:17:36Z; all eight containers ran; the worker validated the model directory and native source hashes before the failure.
classification.external_context_from_lead: The lead reports that a separate CPU-side run reproduced TCPStore/Gloo with rank 0 switching ports while three peers stayed on the old one; that observation shows an internal port-switch behaviour is reachable but does not identify the occupant in this job. It is outside this artifact set.

The receipt script sums only containers that expose state.terminated; at capture time only exp-1102-164536-160317-a87ff679 reported one (1824 s x 8 GPU / 3600 = 4.053333333333334). The other seven replicas were stopped with state.running still reported and therefore contribute nothing to that field. Do not use it as the campaign GPU-hour total; see timing_and_gpu_usage for the exact/estimate split.

withdrawn_suggestions.policy: No remedy in this report is recommended or authorized. The lead owns any bounded source/CPU repair proposal to YC. These drafts were withdrawn after review.

items.suggestion: Pin --data-parallel-master-port to a fixed value per role.
items.withdrawn_because: The nonelastic code path consumes _data_parallel_master_port_list first, so supplying a fixed data_parallel_master_port alone does not establish collision avoidance.

items.suggestion: Run a pre-launch "ss -ltn" audit of the relevant ports on every node.
items.withdrawn_because: It is a time-of-check snapshot; it cannot exclude a port chosen or occupied after the check, nor a race between the native processes themselves.

items.suggestion: Split the 1800 s startup window into a 240-300 s DP-rendezvous deadline and further H200 diagnostic runs.
items.withdrawn_because: The 240-300 s figure is arbitrary and not derived from the evidence; further H200 diagnostic runs are not authorized and would consume scarce capacity without selecting a cause.
